name: Shiretoko
blurb: Sea ice feeds plankton, plankton feeds salmon, and salmon feed bears and fish owls.

tip.title: Melt the sea ice
tip.text: Drift ice releases nutrients that start the plankton bloom. Set Drift sea ice to -100% and watch plankton, then fish, sea lions and eagles.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Drift sea ice
nodes.desc: Ice from the Sea of Okhotsk is carried south each winter and reaches Shiretoko. As it melts in spring it releases nutrients that help start the plankton bloom.

nodes.name: Nutrient-rich deep water
nodes.desc: Currents lift nutrient-rich deep ocean water along the peninsula. Together with melting ice, it fuels spring plankton blooms.

nodes.name: Spawning rivers and streams
nodes.desc: Small, short rivers where salmon and other salmonids return to spawn, carrying ocean nutrients inland.

nodes.name: Forest soil and nutrients
nodes.desc: Soil of the peninsula forests and meadows, enriched by decaying plants and by animals that die or leave remains on land.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and bacteria that break down dead plants, carcasses and spent salmon, returning nutrients to soil.

nodes.name: Sea ice algae and phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae that bloom in spring when sea ice melts and nutrients rise. They are the base of the marine food web.

nodes.name: Bog bilberry
nodes.desc: A low berry shrub of cool northern ground. Its berries are eaten by brown bears, red foxes and voles.

nodes.name: Kuril bamboo grass
nodes.desc: A dwarf bamboo that carpets the forest floor and clearings of Hokkaido, a staple browse for deer.

nodes.name: Mongolian oak
nodes.desc: One of the main trees of the peninsula lowland forests. Its acorns are a food for bears and rodents.

nodes.name: Copepods and zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans that graze the spring bloom and pass its energy on to young salmon and schooling fish.

nodes.name: Sika deer
nodes.desc: A common grazer and browser of the peninsula, eating grasses and dwarf bamboo. Winter deer carcasses feed eagles, crows and bears.

nodes.name: Gray red-backed vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of forest and scrub that eats berries and other plant matter. It is prey for foxes, owls and raptors.

nodes.name: Large Japanese field mouse
nodes.desc: A forest mouse that feeds mainly on seeds and nuts such as acorns, and is prey for many predators.

nodes.name: Walleye pollock
nodes.desc: A schooling cod relative of cold northern seas. It feeds on zooplankton and is key winter food for eagles and sea lions.

nodes.name: Pink and chum salmon
nodes.desc: Feed at sea on plankton and small animals, then return to spawn in the rivers. Their run carries ocean nutrients to bears, owls and the forest.

nodes.name: Steller sea lion
nodes.desc: Winters and springs at haul-outs around Hokkaido. It eats pollock, cod, salmon and squid.

nodes.name: Blakiston's fish owl
nodes.desc: A very large owl of old riverside forest that hunts fish, including salmon, plus frogs and small mammals. It needs rivers that stay partly unfrozen in winter.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: An opportunistic hunter and scavenger that takes voles, birds and berries.

nodes.name: Large-billed crow
nodes.desc: A bold scavenger that feeds on carrion, fish remains and plant foods.

nodes.name: Steller's sea eagle
nodes.desc: A huge eagle that winters on the Okhotsk coast. It eats mainly pollock and cod and readily scavenges carrion such as deer carcasses.

nodes.name: Hokkaido brown bear
nodes.desc: The peninsula holds Japan's densest bear population. It eats berries, acorns, deer and spawning salmon, and carries salmon nutrients into the forest.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: Hunts in the cold waters off the peninsula; recorded prey include sea lions, seals and porpoises.
